text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Opposition Social Democrats no longer insist meeting between Chancellor Helmut Kohl and their leader Oskar Lafontaine is precondition for continuing tax reform talks with government.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel does not rule out further cuts in social policy spending to meet the deficit target for European monetary union (EMU).
- Talks on possible merger between Krupp KFHG.F and Thyssen appear to be making progress, sources say.
- Only a few businesses are prepared for EMU if it starts on time, survey by German Chambers of Industry and Commerce (DIHT) says.
HANDELSBLATT
- Government considering further austerity drive to meet EMU targets.
- Waigel proposes using planned increased in value-added tax to lower labour costs.
- Trio of top managers leaves tour operator LTU after dissatisfaction over their performance.
- Wolfgang Clement, economics minister of North Rhine-Westphalia state, says he expects peaceful solution from talks between Krupp and Thyssen.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bavarian state government and private banks ready to provide more than billion marks in credit for media group Kirch.
- Leading members of Free Democrats, junior coalition partners in government, back Finance Minister Theo Waigel in his row with Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber.
- Government health reforms could provoke challenge in consitutional court, expert says.
- Trade association of skilled workers says 50,000 jobs are under threat in its sector this year.
DIE WELT
- Waigel does not exclude tax rises.
- Lafontaine wants to negotiate with Kohl on health reform plans.
- Steel merger talks would create company called Ruhr Stahl AG, which would solve 70 percent of Krupp and Thyssen's problems, sources close to the talks say.
- Economists criticise government package designed to stimulate investment, especially in construction sector.
